source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: GPT-3 (text-davinci-003) matched or beat UCLA undergraduates on digit matrices, letter-string and verbal analogies, with human-like error patterns.
numbers: Digit Matrices (N=40 humans): GPT-3 above humans, generative OR=1.88 p=0.005; multiple choice OR=6.27 p=2.3e-8. Letter strings (N=57): OR=1.76 p=6.3e-5 overall; accuracy fell with number of generalizations (GPT-3 OR=0.51, humans OR=0.66). Subtype correlation human vs GPT-3 r(39)=0.7.
quote: GPT-3 displayed a surprisingly strong capacity for abstract pattern induction, matching or even surpassing human capabilities in most settings
limits: Best human answered every matrix problem. Letter-string and verbal items may be on the web (authors admit). Digit matrices are text, not vision. Humans were one UCLA student sample.
agent_relevance: Pro side of the debate: a pure text model can do relational mapping on novel-looking items. Treat as an upper bound on what holds in-distribution.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning, verbal and story analogy sections
finding: On four-term verbal analogies GPT-3 was as good as or better than humans; on story analogies it only passed the near (same domain) condition. GPT-4 later did well on the far condition too.
numbers: Verbal: VAT (N=57), Sternberg and Nigro (N=20), SAT items beat estimated high-school average, Jones et al. (N=241) numerically weaker but in range. Semantic distance effect in GPT-3 OR=3.24 p=0.0165. Story analogy: GPT-3 reliable only near; GPT-4 near-perfect near and much stronger far (72 problems).
limits: Items scored by log probability of each answer option, not free generation. No memorisation found by probing, but probing is weak evidence.
agent_relevance: Relational transfer across domains (far analogy) is where weaker models fail; a scaffold that restates problems abstractly may help weaker backbones.

source: Lewis and Mitchell (2024) Using counterfactual tasks to evaluate the generality of analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Humans stay high on letter-string analogies with permuted alphabets; GPT-3, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 drop sharply. Failed replication of the claim that GPT matches humans.
numbers: Humans: 136 Prolific participants, 1,876 samples, mean accuracy 0.753 [0.734,0.773], flat across 0,2,5,10,20 permuted letters. GPT models, 6,840 samples each, means about 0.35 to 0.49 (table column alignment in the PDF text is garbled; text says GPT-3.5 is worse than GPT-3 and GPT-4 no better). On the original alphabet GPT accuracy was below the human average, unlike Webb.
quote: GPT models' performance declines sharply on the counterfactual set
limits: Zero-generalization problems only. Prompt format borrowed from Hodel and West was best. Comprehension checks (successor/predecessor in the new alphabet) were mostly high, so models understood the task statement.
agent_relevance: Strong reason to test our O7 analogy operator on counterfactual surface forms, not only on familiar ones.

source: Lewis and Mitchell (2024) error analysis and conclusions
finding: Error types differ. Humans often find a valid alternative rule, GPT-3 rarely. Chat tuning may have hurt: GPT-3.5 was worse than GPT-3 and GPT-4 no better.
numbers: Error shares, GPT-3 / GPT-4 / human: alternate valid rule 5.81% / 22.00% / 38.59%; incorrect rule 30.97% / 32.67% / 14.67%; wrong 55.48% / 42.67% / 34.24%; completely wrong 7.74% / 2.67% / 12.50%. About 160 errors per model, 184 human.
limits: Small hand-coded samples; coding by the authors. Chat-tuning explanation is their guess.
agent_relevance: Checking for a valid alternative rule is a human signature. A scaffold can ask for a second mapping and score both.

source: Hodel and West (2023) Response: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Simple variants of the letter-string tasks (synthetic alphabet, larger interval) break GPT-3 while humans stay high. Argues the zero-shot claim is unproven because items may be in training data.
numbers: GPT-3 generative accuracy below 0.1 on the synthetic alphabet for extend, successor, predecessor, fix; only remove-redundant and sort stay in the original range. Human group N=121 UW undergraduates, same accuracy as on original items.
limits: The first author of the original had predicted the modified tasks would also be harder for humans; they were not. Human sample is students.
agent_relevance: Do not accept a benchmark pass as proof of a general relational skill. Add surface-changed twins of each test.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2024) Evidence from counterfactual tasks supports emergent analogical reasoning in LLMs
finding: Reply: GPT-4 with code execution solves the permuted-alphabet task at human level; the failure is counting letter positions, not relational reasoning. Without code GPT-4 is significantly worse than humans.
numbers: GPT-4 (gpt-4-0125-preview) plain: humans better. GPT-4 + code execution vs humans: P=0.496 (no difference). 46% of GPT-4 errors used a valid alternative rule vs 39% in human data of Lewis and Mitchell. 300 problems at interval 1.
quote: the inability of language models to solve these problems stems from a specific difficulty with counting
limits: Not independent or preregistered. Hand-graded verbose outputs. Code use is not a human-like route.
agent_relevance: Supports our design: the program counts and indexes, the model supplies the relation. Counting failures should not be read as relational failures.

source: Musker, Duchnowski, Millière, Pavlick (2025) LLMs as models for analogical reasoning (J Mem Lang 145)
finding: Semantic structure-mapping tasks (words mapped to symbol strings). Best models (GPT-4, Claude 3 Opus, Llama-405B) match humans in the default condition but differ in distractor handling and in generalising 2x2 structures to larger ones.
numbers: 194 mostly Brown undergraduates in total. Default condition: no significant gap for GPT-4 (p=0.097), Claude 3 (p=0.194), Llama-405B (p=0.097). Generalised structure: GPT-4 and Llama drop significantly, Claude 3 stays human level. Semantic content with numeric properties: humans and Claude 3 about 0.7 match to reference; GPT-4 and Llama-405B about 0.35 (GPT-4 p=0.002). Weak models fail (Falcon-40B 0.1, GPT-3 0.5 match).
limits: Match to reference answer, not accuracy, since answers are not unique. Models differ from each other, so no single model stands for the human.
agent_relevance: Model choice matters. Random irrelevant words hurt models more than humans: screen context for distractors before mapping.

source: Moskvichev, Odouard, Mitchell (2023) The ConceptARC benchmark
finding: On 16 concept groups of simple visual relational concepts humans beat top ARC-Kaggle programs and GPT-4.
numbers: Humans over 90% on 11 of 16 concepts and over 80% on the other 5. First-place ARC-Kaggle program never above 80%, below 60% on 11 of 16, average gap 40 points. Second place below 50% on 15 of 16. GPT-4 below 30% on 15 of 16 (33% on one).
limits: GPT-4 was text-only, 2023 version. Newer reasoning models not measured here.
agent_relevance: Core relational concepts in grids were weak for text models in 2023. Our scaffold should verify with code, not intuition.

source: Qiu et al. (2024) Phenomenal yet puzzling: testing inductive reasoning of LMs with hypothesis refinement (ICLR)
finding: LMs propose good candidate rules but struggle to apply them. Iterative hypothesis refinement with a symbolic interpreter gives the strongest result on 3 of 4 datasets, but accuracy collapses on counterfactual variants.
numbers: Task accuracy dropped from more than 80% to almost zero on counterfactual MiniSCAN variants (text). Human rule-writing comparison on 50 tasks each for List Functions and MiniARC.
limits: Humans not tested in every LM setup (authors' footnote). Other table numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Hybrid pattern the schema already uses: model proposes rule, program applies and checks.

source: Qiu et al. (2024) rule application gap
finding: Models write plausible rules but cannot always apply their own rules; humans abstract away surface forms, models do not.
numbers: Gap statements only; per-table percentages not read.
limits: Numbers partly unread.
agent_relevance: Never let the model apply its own rule without a program check.

source: A Dissociative Framework for Understanding Same-Different Conceptualization (2021 review)
finding: Species differences in relational matching are read through an explicit-declarative vs implicit-procedural learning split: humans explicit, language-trained apes partly, macaques intermediate, pigeons little.
numbers: Humans up to 99% on RMTS, often with sudden insight. Macaques: none succeeded over 260,000 trials of cue fading. Baboons (Fagot and Thompson): 6 of 29 reached 80% after 15,000 to 30,000 trials. Baboons matched multi-item arrays with a visual entropy cue; with object pairs performance collapsed. Wide spatial separation of colour pairs also collapsed baboon performance.
limits: A theory-advocating review. Explicit-declarative labels are inferred, not measured in animals.
agent_relevance: Rival to Penn et al.: not 'no relational ability' but dependence on working-memory-heavy explicit reconstrual. Suggests explicit restatement steps.

source: Thompson, Flemming, Hagmann (2016) Can old-world and new-world monkeys judge spatial above/below relations to be the same or different?
finding: Failed replications of relational matching in monkeys. Rhesus never exceeded chance. Capuchins exceeded chance only without Clever Hans controls.
numbers: Rhesus: none above chance over 10,000 training trials. Capuchins: above chance only in sessions 14 and 15, run without opaque screens. Mean about 198 trials per session (range 128 to 352).
limits: Small samples typical of primate work; failures may reflect colony and procedure.
agent_relevance: Results that vanish when cueing is controlled. Always run a no-cue control when testing our own agent.

source: Same paper: history of RMTS scaffolds (tokens, differential outcomes)
finding: Tokens helped language-trained chimpanzees; token training had no scaffolding effect on rhesus (Flemming 2008). Differential outcomes gave rhesus transitory two-item RMTS (Flemming 2011).
numbers: Only 6 of 29 baboons acquired two-item RMTS (Fagot and Thompson 2011). Truppa 2011 and Fagot 2001 are cited as negative for pair-based performance.
limits: Second-hand summaries from the authors' introduction.
agent_relevance: External symbols help relational judgement in apes; same logic as giving an LLM explicit labels for relations.

source: Smirnova, Zorina, Obozova, Wasserman (2015) Crows spontaneously exhibit analogical reasoning (Curr Biol 25)
finding: Crows matched relations (same or different pairs) after only identity matching training, a spontaneous relational transfer.
numbers: Abstract only; N and percentages not recorded.
limits: Only the abstract record was read. Numbers need the paper.
agent_relevance: Counter-evidence to a strict human-only gap: birds succeed without relational training.

source: Penn, Holyoak, Povinelli (2008) Darwin's mistake (BBS 31)
finding: Claims a discontinuity in higher-order, systematic relational ability (a physical symbol system) between humans and animals, and points to symbolic-connectionist models.
numbers: Abstract only; no numbers.
limits: Full article and commentaries not opened; later crow and parrot RMTS data are cited elsewhere as challenges.
agent_relevance: Frames the gap behind O7 background. Not verified in detail.

source: Breaking the perceptual-conceptual barrier: relational matching and working memory (2019)
finding: A concurrent working-memory load stopped humans from moving from a perceptual cue to the abstract relational solution unless the load was dropped.
numbers: Experiment 1: 120 Georgia State undergraduates; analysed 53 Control and 51 Concurrent-load. Humans in the unloaded fading task were 99% correct overall.
limits: Students only; final transition rates not extracted.
agent_relevance: Moderator: load. Discovering a relation is working-memory-bound even in humans. Keep context lean when asking an agent to infer a relation.

source: Endpoint distinctiveness facilitates analogical mapping in pigeons (2015)
finding: Pigeons trained with ordinal size-to-position mapping learned faster than random mapping, but the advantage came from endpoint distinctiveness and proximity errors, not a relational map.
numbers: 3 pigeons mapped, 3 random; six alternatives; 70 reassignment sessions of 60 trials. Mean error distance 1.15 positions (ordered) vs 1.73 (random). No speed difference after reversal.
limits: Six birds.
agent_relevance: A reversal test separates relation from cue. Use reversal tests on agent analogies.

source: Relational complexity influences analogical reasoning ability (2023, iScience)
finding: A language-free analogy task for cross-species use: humans learn quickly, performance falls with analogy complexity and correlates with fluid intelligence.
numbers: Criterion (5 consecutive correct) reached in 20.2 +/- 0.86 trials; transfer accuracy 0.82 +/- 0.02, many at ceiling.
limits: Human-only data; offered as a tool for later animal work.
agent_relevance: Complexity is a measurable moderator. Report agent accuracy by relational arity.

source: Same paper, framing of the gap
finding: Argues part of the human-animal gap may be a testing artefact, since verbal analogies cannot be given to animals; cites RMTS success in chimpanzees, baboons, crows and parrots.
numbers: No new numbers.
limits: Second-hand description.
agent_relevance: If the gap partly reflects test format, an LLM's pass or fail also depends on format.

source: Hochmann (2022) Representations of abstract relations in infancy (Open Mind 6)
finding: Ten- to 12-month-olds represent 'same' only up to about four items. They fail at 5 or 6 syllables and fail to form an 'all same' representation across varying numbers.
numbers: Six pupillometry experiments, N=192. Four items: generalised (Exp 1 and 4). Five or six: failed (Exp 2 and 3). All-same across numbers: failed (Exp 5 and 6).
quote: infants' representation of the relation same is constrained by the limits of working memory capacity
limits: Preverbal infants; pupillometry is indirect.
agent_relevance: Relations are built from entities, so capacity limits matter. Chunk long relation sets before comparing.

source: Zhu (2025) Preschoolers represent abstract relations predicated on kind membership (Open Mind 9)
finding: Four-year-olds fail relational match-to-sample with familiar kinds at baseline. Noun-label training fixes it for 4 and 5 year olds but not 3 year olds; adjective labels do not help.
numbers: n=192 US preschoolers over three experiments.
limits: Predominantly White, upper-middle-class US convenience sample.
agent_relevance: A short noun-label step can unlock relational choice. Naming the relation is a cheap scaffold.

source: Relational reasoning across cultures: South Korea, US and China (2026)
finding: Korean 18 to 30 month olds infer 'same' like US and Chinese toddlers. From age 3 Korean children show no bias, unlike US (object bias) and Chinese (relational bias) children.
numbers: Study 1: 91 toddlers; same condition 28 of 41 correct (68%, BF10=4.07); different condition 25 of 50 (50%, BF10=0.33, chance). Experiment 2: 55 Korean 3 to 4 year olds and 60 adults.
limits: Cultural moderator. 'Different' not inferred at this age.
agent_relevance: Early 'same' is robust, 'different' is harder. Test both directions in agent relation checks.

source: Lewis and Mitchell (2024) comprehension checks
finding: Models mostly understand the permuted alphabet yet still fail the analogy. GPT-3.5 struggled with predecessor in alphabets with 2 or 5 letters permuted.
numbers: GPT-3.5 predecessor on unpermuted pairs: 0.49 at n=2 and 0.72 at n=5; GPT-4 mostly 0.93 to 1.00. 28 to 175 letter pairs per cell.
limits: PDF table extraction was messy; read with care.
agent_relevance: Add a comprehension check before relational mapping in unfamiliar notation.

source: Webb et al. (2023) supplement: contamination checks
finding: Authors searched for memorised materials and found none but lacked training data access. GPT-4 was tested only on story analogies.
numbers: 72 story problems for GPT-4; context cleared per problem. No GPT-4 matrix or letter-string results (no API at the time).
limits: Absence-of-evidence check; Hodel and West call it weak.
agent_relevance: Contamination cannot be excluded. Use freshly generated items.

source: Hodel and West (2023) argument on human parity and mechanism
finding: Matching a human score does not show the same mechanism. The child versus adult example shows score gaps can mislead.
numbers: No new numbers.
limits: Opinion by the authors.
agent_relevance: Judge by robustness to surface change, not by score parity.
